edges.description: Loss of neurofibromin RAS-GAP activity increases RAS effector signaling.
Germline NF1 heterozygosity creates the single-hit background in which somatic inactivation of the remaining wild-type NF1 allele yields biallelic loss in Schwann-lineage cells.
RAS-MAPK hyperactivation drives cafe-au-lait macule and freckling formation.
RAS-MAPK hyperactivation in the Schwann cell lineage initiates neurofibromas.
Excess RAS-MAPK signaling in optic pathway glial progenitors predisposes to low-grade optic nerve glioma.
Excess RAS-MAPK signaling perturbs growth, craniofacial, and cardiac development.
Hyperactive melanocyte pigmentation programs produce multiple cutaneous cafe-au-lait macules.
Hyperactive cutaneous melanocytes generate axillary and inguinal intertriginous freckling.
Melanocytic proliferation in the iris stroma produces Lisch nodules.
Biallelic NF1 loss in Schwann-lineage cells abolishes neurofibromin RAS-GAP restraint and initiates neurofibroma formation.
Dysregulated RAS-MAPK signaling in NF1-deficient peripheral nerve sheath Schwann cells drives cutaneous and subcutaneous neurofibroma formation.
Early developmental biallelic NF1 loss in nerve-plexus Schwann-lineage cells produces plexiform neurofibromas.
A small subset of plexiform neurofibromas undergo malignant progression upon acquiring cooperating somatic tumor-suppressor alterations.
Developmental RAS-MAPK dysregulation impairs postnatal linear growth.
Dysregulated RAS-MAPK developmental signaling causes relative or absolute macrocephaly.
Craniofacial RAS-MAPK developmental perturbation produces ocular hypertelorism.
Craniofacial and oculomotor developmental perturbation in the RASopathy program leads to congenital ptosis.
Craniofacial morphogenesis altered by excess RAS-MAPK signaling produces downslanted palpebral fissures.
Branchial and craniofacial developmental dysregulation leads to low-set, posteriorly rotated ears.
Developmental lymphatic and cervical soft-tissue remodeling produces a broad or webbed neck.
Altered thoracic wall skeletal morphogenesis produces pectus excavatum or carinatum.
Excess ERK signaling during endocardial cushion and valve morphogenesis causes pulmonic valve stenosis.
Developmental axial skeletal dysplasia in the NF1/RASopathy program predisposes to scoliosis.
Perturbed neuronal RAS-MAPK signaling during brain development impairs cognitive and learning performance.
Developmental RAS-MAPK dysregulation in frontostriatal and cortical circuits predisposes to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
Perturbed neuronal and synaptic RAS-MAPK signaling during neurodevelopment causes developmental delay or intellectual disability in a subset of patients.

nodes.description: Germline heterozygous NF1 loss-of-function variants reduce neurofibromin dosage. Neurofibromin is a RAS-GTPase activating protein (RAS-GAP) that accelerates hydrolysis of active RAS-GTP to inactive RAS-GDP. Reduced neurofibromin function removes this negative restraint on RAS, the shared initiating lesion of NFNS.
